text: permute(seed) and sample(m, seed) both return Drawn<I>, which holds a feisty::Permutation over 0..len() plus a count to keep, so neither allocates a vector. sample keeps the first m positions of the same permutation permute keeps whole, so two draws from one collection under one seed nest. Both take a u64 rather than an Rng so a draw reproduces from its recorded seed alone. Drawn hands positions back in permutation order, so the reads are just as scattered: this saves allocation, not locality.
